hw_components.name: comma device (comma 3X)
hw_components.power_domain: 12 V harness, through the device's own regulators
hw_components.notes: Consumer-grade hardware, no safety rating. Hosts openpilot, driver monitoring, cameras, display and speaker.

hw_components.name: panda board inside the device (tres)
hw_components.part: STM32H725 MCU (Arm Cortex-M7, single core, no lockstep); FDCAN transceivers
hw_components.power_domain: 12 V harness through the device; separate regulator from the SoC
hw_components.clock_domain: 25 MHz HSE crystal with the clock security system on; LSI available for an independent watchdog
hw_components.notes: Executes the safety firmware. Shares the device enclosure, and so its thermal and EMC environment, with HW01.

hw_components.name: Harness box and intercept relay
hw_components.power_domain: Relay coil driven from the panda over the harness cable (SBU lines)
hw_components.notes: De-energized relay passes the stock ADAS camera through to the car: the safe state. Today a stuck-on drive pin keeps the relay closed.

hw_components.name: Relay supervisor (proposed, G1 layer 2)
hw_components.part: To design: AC-coupled charge-pump coil driver in the harness box
hw_components.power_domain: From the relay drive itself; no stored energy beyond one release time
hw_components.clock_domain: Toggle signal from a panda timer, gated by the safety firmware
hw_components.notes: Keeps the relay closed only while it receives a correctly toggling signal. A stuck-high or stuck-low pin, a hung MCU or a reset all open the relay.

hw_components.name: Vehicle 12 V supply and harness wiring
hw_components.notes: Loss de-energizes the relay and powers down both device and panda.

hw_components.name: Vehicle actuators (outside the item)
hw_components.part: Vehicle EPS, powertrain and brake ECUs
hw_components.notes: Covered by platform assumptions ASM-V-01, ASM-V-02 and ASM-V-07.

sw_partitions.name: openpilot driving stack (modeld, plannerd, controlsd, car controllers)
sw_partitions.notes: The doer. Bounds its own commands to the same limits, but nothing in the safety argument for SG-001 to SG-005 relies on it.

sw_partitions.name: selfdrived, alerts and UI
sw_partitions.notes: Carries the take-over and state-display requirements of SG-006, SG-007 and SG-009. Developed as QM today: TSC gap T1.

sw_partitions.name: Driver monitoring (dmonitoringmodeld, dmonitoringd)
sw_partitions.notes: Carries SG-008. Learned model plus alert policy; developed as QM today: TSC gap T1. ISO/PAS 8800 applies to the model.

sw_partitions.name: panda safety firmware: brand safety modes
sw_partitions.notes: opendbc/safety. The checker. Treated as existing software (ISO 26262-8 §12) until LionDriver verification closes.

sw_partitions.name: panda platform firmware: main loop, drivers, comms, fault handling
sw_partitions.notes: Shares the MCU with SP04 without memory protection, so it must be developed to D or shown not to interfere (DFA). Hosts the proposed G1 measures.

sw_partitions.name: panda bootstub
sw_partitions.notes: Verifies the RSA signature of the application before jumping to it.

corrections_to_fsc: Node N07 is named 'USB link' in the FSC. On the comma 3X the internal panda is reached over SPI, with an 8-bit XOR checksum on every frame from the device, a CRC-8 on the panda's responses, and ACK/NACK handshakes (panda board/drivers/spi.h). External pandas use USB. The requirements are unchanged; the next FSC revision should rename the node.

g1.title: panda microcontroller fault detection
finding: Crash-type faults already reach the safe state: HardFault and NMI handlers reset the MCU (board/early_init.h), the firmware starts in SILENT with the relay de-energized (board/main.c set_safety_mode at startup), and an HSE clock failure raises an NMI through the clock security system (board/stm32h7/clock.h).

Every other detected fault is only recorded. fault_occurred() sets a bit in the health packet (board/sys/faults.h). The heartbeat-loop watchdog, the 1 Hz register-divergence check, interrupt-rate monitoring and the unused-interrupt handler all end there. Nothing blocks output, and openpilot acts only on relayMalfunction (selfdrived.py).

There is no independent hardware watchdog. IND_WDG is defined as IWDG1 in stm32h7_config.h but never started. A firmware hang with interrupts still running, or with the relay drive pin latched high, leaves the relay closed.
The STM32H7 has ECC on flash and RAM, but the firmware neither enables nor handles ECC error reporting (the ECC interrupt has no registered handler), so memory errors are not acted on.
The Cortex-M7 is single core without lockstep. A silent computation error, such as a bit flip in a limiter variable, is not detected by any current mechanism.

layers.name: Firmware measures on the existing panda
layers.summary: Turn recorded faults into a latched no-output state, start the independent watchdog with program-flow checks, enable ECC reporting, protect critical safety state with inverted copies, and check code and RAM integrity.

layers.name: Independent disable path: relay supervisor
layers.status: Proposed; needs a harness-box hardware change
layers.summary: Energize the relay only from a correctly toggling signal through an AC-coupled driver, so that any stuck pin, hang or reset opens the relay without help from the MCU.

layers.name: Diverse monitoring MCU
layers.summary: A second microcontroller from a different family in the harness box, reading vehicle CAN on its own and able to open the relay. It checks a minimal set: steering torque magnitude and rate, and no actuation while the brake is pressed. This makes the checker a two-channel design.

g1.decision_rule: Implement L1, design L2, then run the panda FMEDA (WP-HW-01). ASIL D needs a single-point fault metric of at least 99 %, a latent fault metric of at least 90 % and a PMHF below 10 FIT (ISO 26262-5 §8–9). If L1 + L2 cannot reach those numbers on a single non-lockstep core, add L3 or revisit the controllability ratings that make SG-001 to SG-005 ASIL D (HARA review note).

mechanisms.name: Command limit checks (torque/angle magnitude, rate, deviation from measurement, change per 250 ms; acceleration range)
mechanisms.reaction: Block the frame and reset the limiter state

mechanisms.name: Engagement and release logic (cruise rising edge, brake, gas, cruise falling edge)
mechanisms.reaction: Clear controls_allowed; every actuating frame is then blocked

mechanisms.name: Vehicle message integrity: checksum, counter, quality flag, timeout
mechanisms.detection: Checksum and counter per frame; timeout within 2 s (1 Hz check, 1 s lag threshold)
mechanisms.dc: TBD; per-message protection depends on the vehicle

mechanisms.name: Device link supervision: SPI frame checksum, engagement agreement, heartbeat timeout
mechanisms.detection: Checksum per frame; 3 s engagement mismatch; 5 s heartbeat loss (ignition on)
mechanisms.reaction: Drop the frame; clear controls_allowed; enter SILENT with the relay de-energized and sound the siren

mechanisms.name: Transmit whitelist (address, bus, length)
mechanisms.reaction: Block the frame, count it in safety_tx_blocked

mechanisms.name: Relay malfunction detection (stock ECU message seen while intercepting)
mechanisms.detection: First stock-ECU frame on an intercepted address
mechanisms.reaction: Latch relay_malfunction, block all output, openpilot raises relayMalfunction

mechanisms.name: Safety mode selection with SILENT fallback and mode agreement
mechanisms.detection: On every mode change; agreement checked continuously by openpilot
mechanisms.reaction: Fall back to SILENT; openpilot disengages on mismatch

mechanisms.name: Crash reset to SILENT (HardFault, NMI, HSE clock failure)
mechanisms.reaction: System reset; firmware starts in SILENT, relay de-energized

mechanisms.name: Signed-firmware check at boot
mechanisms.reaction: Refuse to start an unsigned application

mechanisms.name: Fault escalation to latched no-output
mechanisms.reaction: Clear controls_allowed, enter NOOUTPUT with the relay de-energized, latch until power cycle

mechanisms.name: Independent watchdog (IWDG1, LSI clock) with program-flow monitoring
mechanisms.dc: TBD; typical 90–95 % for processor and software faults
mechanisms.where: New; IND_WDG already defined in stm32h7_config.h

mechanisms.name: Inverted copies of critical safety state
Runtime code CRC and startup RAM test
mechanisms.detection: Code: full pass within 1 s using the hardware CRC unit. RAM: at startup before the relay can be driven
mechanisms.reaction: Fault escalation (SM-FLT); at startup, stay in SILENT

mechanisms.name: Relay supervisor: dynamic (toggling) coil drive
mechanisms.detection: Loss of toggling, proposed within 20 ms

mechanisms.name: Take-over and state alerts (device), siren on heartbeat loss (panda)
mechanisms.reaction: Audible and visual alert; panda siren for 3 s when the device stops responding while engaged

mechanisms.name: Driver monitoring escalation
mechanisms.detection: Distraction 5 s / 8 s / 13 s; uncertainty fallback to wheel touch 5 / 15 / 25 s after 10 s
mechanisms.reaction: Visual, then audible alert, then disengage with lockout

mechanisms.name: Supply loss and brown-out
mechanisms.detection: Brown-out reset level in the MCU option bytes
mechanisms.reaction: Relay de-energizes on supply loss; MCU held in reset below the brown-out level
mechanisms.status: Existing by design; BOR level to verify

tsrs.text: For torque-steering vehicles, the safety mode shall forward a steering frame only if controls are allowed and the commanded torque is within ±max_torque, its change from the previous command is within max_rate_up / max_rate_down, it is within max_torque_error of the measured EPS torque (or the driver-torque allowance), and its change over the last 250 ms is within max_rt_delta. Any other frame shall be blocked and the limiter state reset.

For angle-steering vehicles, the safety mode shall forward an angle command only if controls are allowed and the angle and its rate are within the speed-dependent limits relative to the measured steering angle; any other frame shall be blocked.
While controls are not allowed, the only steering frames forwarded shall be those with zero torque and the steer-request bit cleared.
Speed-dependent limits shall use the minimum of the last six vehicle-speed samples.

The safety mode shall forward an acceleration request other than the inactive value only while controls are allowed, the gas pedal was not pressed on the previous frame, and the request is within [min_accel, max_accel] (Toyota −3.5 to +2.0 m/s²); otherwise the frame shall be blocked.
On vehicles in stock-longitudinal configuration, the only longitudinal frame forwarded shall be the cruise cancel request.
tsrs.where: Brand safety modes (tx whitelist per configuration)

tsrs.text: Evaluate a limit on the rate of change of the commanded deceleration, so that a valid but sudden request cannot step from cruising to the maximum deceleration in one frame. Decide together with the SOTIF analysis of phantom braking (G4).
The safety mode shall set controls_allowed only on the rising edge of the vehicle's stock cruise-engaged signal, and clear it whenever that signal is false.
The safety mode shall clear controls_allowed on the rising edge of the brake pedal, and whenever the brake is pressed while the vehicle is moving.

tsrs.status: Existing upstream; to confirm by review
tsrs.text: No message from the device shall be able to set controls_allowed. Only the safety mode's receive path may set it.
tsrs.where: controls_allowed writers: safety.h pcm_cruise_check and brand modes; to confirm by code review of main_comms.h

tsrs.text: For every message in the safety mode's receive-check table, the safety mode shall validate the checksum, counter and quality flag where the vehicle provides them, and clear controls_allowed on any failure.

tsrs.status: Existing upstream; timing to verify against FTTI
tsrs.text: The safety mode shall clear controls_allowed when a receive-checked message has not arrived within max(1 s, 10 periods). The check runs at 1 Hz, so detection takes up to 2 s. If the FTTI (G2) is shorter, the check shall run faster or per message.

Where the vehicle provides no checksum or counter on a message the safety mode relies on (Toyota brake pedal), the configuration shall show that the vehicle-side integrity meets assumption ASM-V-03, or add a plausibility check against a second signal.

The panda shall discard device frames that fail their 8-bit XOR checksum and answer with NACK. An XOR checksum misses some multi-bit errors, so a corrupted command that passes it is still subject to TSR-LIM and TSR-TX; whether a CRC is needed is left to the DFA and FMEDA.
The panda shall clear controls_allowed when the device's heartbeat reports disengaged for 3 consecutive seconds while controls are allowed.
The panda shall enter SILENT, de-energizing the relay, after 5 s without a heartbeat with ignition on (2 s with ignition off), and sound the siren for 3 s if controls were allowed in the last 5 s.
The panda shall transmit only frames whose address, bus and length are on the active safety mode's whitelist, and block and count all others.
The safety mode shall latch relay_malfunction when a frame on an intercepted address arrives from the stock ECU side, and block all output while it is latched; openpilot shall raise relayMalfunction.

The relay coil shall be energized only through an AC-coupled driver fed by a toggling signal (proposed 1 kHz) from a panda timer. The relay shall de-energize within 20 ms (to confirm against the FTTI) of the signal stopping or sticking high or low. The supervisor shall need no software to open the relay.

The firmware shall enable the relay toggle signal only from the 8 Hz tick, after the program-flow check of TSR-MCU-06 passes, and only in a car safety mode with no latched fault. It shall stop the toggle in every other case.

tsrs.status: Existing by design; release time to measure
tsrs.text: A de-energized relay shall connect the stock ADAS camera to the car. Its release time shall be measured and included in every FRTI.
The panda shall fall back to SILENT when setting the requested safety mode fails, and halt if SILENT itself cannot be set.
openpilot shall disengage and block engagement when the panda's reported safety mode or parameter differs from the one requested, or its receive checks are invalid.
HardFault and NMI shall reset the MCU, and the firmware shall start in SILENT with the relay de-energized.
The HSE clock security system shall be enabled, so that a crystal failure raises an NMI and resets the MCU.
The bootstub shall start the application only if its RSA signature verifies against the release key (or the debug key on development units).

On any of FAULT_HEARTBEAT_LOOP_WATCHDOG, FAULT_REGISTER_DIVERGENT, FAULT_UNUSED_INTERRUPT_HANDLED, the CAN, tick, interrupt-timer and SPI interrupt-rate faults, or an uncorrectable ECC error, the firmware shall clear controls_allowed and enter NOOUTPUT with the relay de-energized, latched until power cycle. Today these faults are only recorded.

The independent watchdog (IWDG1, clocked from the LSI, independent of the HSE and PLL) shall be started by hardware through the option bytes, so software cannot disable it. Its timeout shall be 250 ms (to confirm against the FTTI). On expiry the MCU shall reset into SILENT.

The firmware shall refresh the watchdog only from the 8 Hz tick, and only when every program-flow checkpoint expected since the last refresh has been passed: safety receive hook, safety_tick (each second), and the transmit hook whenever frames were sent.

Flash and RAM ECC error reporting shall be enabled and the ECC interrupt registered. A double-bit error shall trigger TSR-MCU-04. Single-bit corrections shall be counted and reported in the health packet.

controls_allowed, the active safety mode and parameter, relay_malfunction and the steering limiter state shall each be stored with a bit-inverted copy, checked on every transmit check; a mismatch shall trigger TSR-MCU-04.

The firmware shall compute a CRC-32 over the application code with the hardware CRC unit, incrementally, completing a full pass at least once per second, and trigger TSR-MCU-04 on mismatch with the value stored at build time.
At startup, before any car safety mode can be set, the firmware shall run a March-type test over the RAM holding safety state and stay in SILENT if it fails.
The brown-out reset level shall be set in the option bytes so that the MCU is held in reset whenever its supply is too low for correct execution.

openpilot shall disengage with an alert and block engagement whenever the panda reports a fault status other than none. This is diagnostic coverage on the QM side; the safety argument relies on TSR-MCU-04, not on this.
Loss of the 12 V harness supply shall de-energize the relay and power down the panda and device, leaving the car in stock behavior.
openpilot's car controllers shall apply the same limits as the safety mode, so that the panda acts as a backstop and blocks frames only after a fault.
openpilot shall raise an audible and visual take-over request within a specified time (TBD from the FTTI of SG-006) whenever lateral control is lost, saturated or about to end.
Take-over requests shall stay active until the driver acknowledges them or the system disengages.
openpilot shall raise an audible take-over request when the required deceleration exceeds what it may command.
tsrs.where: selfdrive alerts (forward collision warning, brake hold)

tsrs.text: The displayed engagement state shall agree with the panda's controls_allowed; on disagreement openpilot shall disengage with an alert. Engagement and disengagement shall each be signaled audibly and visually.

tsrs.status: Existing upstream; to verify on the comma 3X
tsrs.text: The panda shall sound its siren when the device stops sending heartbeats while controls were allowed, so that the driver is warned even if the device has failed.
tsrs.where: panda board/main.c siren_countdown; on the comma 3X (tres) the siren is generated by the panda through the device's audio amplifier over I2C (board/boards/tres.h fake_i2c_siren_set), so it shares the speaker with the device

tsrs.text: Driver monitoring shall escalate a visual alert, an audible alert and a disengagement with lockout at 5 s, 8 s and 13 s of distraction, and fall back to the 5 / 15 / 25 s wheel-touch policy after 10 s of model uncertainty.
Loss or degradation of the driver camera shall block engagement and disengage an active system with an alert.

hsi.integrity: 8-bit XOR checksum per frame (weak against multi-bit errors)

hsi.reaction: 3 s mismatch: controls off; 5 s missing: SILENT

hsi.integrity: Inside CRC-protected frame; echoed back in health

hsi.encoding: Status byte (none / temporary / permanent) + 32-bit fault bitmask
hsi.reaction: Today: logged only (relay malfunction excepted). Proposed: disengage and block engagement

hsi.encoding: Counters and flag in health packet
GPIO level today; proposed 1 kHz square wave
hsi.integrity: Proposed: AC coupling rejects a static level
hsi.reaction: Loss of toggle de-energizes the relay

hsi.rate: 8 Hz tick, gated by program-flow check
hsi.integrity: Key sequence; LSI clock independent of HSE/PLL

hsi.encoding: Siren tone through the device audio amplifier (I2C, tres)
hsi.rate: On heartbeat loss while engaged, 3 s
hsi.reaction: Audible warning independent of the device

timing.frti: Next steering frame blocked (≤ 10 ms at 100 Hz)
timing.notes: Plus EPS ramp-down, outside the item.
Likely too slow against a lateral FTTI. Candidate for a faster check (TSR-RX-02).
Covers a device that stopped engaging; limits still apply during the 3 s.
Limits still apply during the 5 s; this mainly ends output from a dead device.
GPIOs go to their reset state immediately, so the relay drive drops at reset.
Timeout to set from the FTTI.
Independent of firmware and of the MCU clock tree.

timing.fdti: As the underlying monitor (register check 1 s; loop watchdog 375 ms; ECC immediate)
timing.frti: Next tick (≤ 125 ms) + relay release time
timing.notes: Register check at 1 Hz may need to run faster.

dfa.pair: SG-001 to SG-005 / N14 panda safety firmware (checker, D(D)) / N11 openpilot driving software (doer, QM(D))

rows.mitigation: Total loss de-energizes the relay (safe state). Partial loss: brown-out reset holds the MCU in reset (TSR-MCU-11, to verify).
Ground loss behaves as supply loss for both elements and the relay.
SoC and MCU have separate clock sources; the MCU's HSE is supervised by the clock security system.

rows.present: Yes: the SPI link carries every command
rows.mitigation: The checker validates every command it carries (TSR-LIM, TSR-TX); 8-bit XOR checksum per frame; silence triggers the heartbeat timeout.

rows.present: Yes: both use the same vehicle CAN signals (speed, EPS torque, pedals, cruise)
rows.mitigation: Checksums, counters and timeouts where the vehicle provides them (TSR-RX-01/02). A wrong but valid vehicle signal affects both: relies on assumptions ASM-V-03 and ASM-V-05. Toyota brake has no checksum (G5).
Separate chips; no shared RAM or flash.

rows.present: Partly: both sides' limit values come from the same opendbc repository and team
rows.mitigation: A wrong limit would be wrong in both. Limits must trace to vehicle-level validation (G2), not to each other. The XZACT re-implementation checks the C code, not the values.
Linux on the SoC; bare metal on the MCU.

rows.present: Yes: the panda sits inside the device enclosure
rows.mitigation: Over-temperature or EMC affecting both must lead to the safe state. Needs environmental qualification of the panda in the device (heat soak, EMC).

rows.present: Yes: both developed upstream by comma.ai
rows.mitigation: Independent verification of the checker by LionDriver: XZACT diverse implementation, mutation testing, independent review once reviewers are recruited (A01).
arm-none-eabi-gcc for the panda; Python, clang and tinygrad on the device. The panda compiler is classified TCL3 in the safety plan.
The checker has its own test suite (opendbc safety tests with mutation analysis) and the XZACT equivalence harness, separate from process replay.

dfa.conclusion: Mitigation in progress. Three factors are open (shared limit values, shared environmental zone, and G1 itself through the shared MCU of SP04 and SP05). The D(D) + QM(D) decomposition stays proposed, not claimed.

gaps.title: panda microcontroller fault detection
gaps.status: Design proposed (L1 firmware, L2 relay supervisor); FMEDA decides L3
gaps.next: Implement L1 in LionDriver's panda fork with fault-injection tests; design the relay supervisor; FMEDA (WP-HW-01).

gaps.title: FTTIs not set
gaps.status: Open; TSC timing table lists each mechanism's detection and reaction time
gaps.next: Vehicle tests on the reference Corolla; then set the watchdog, supervisor and receive-timeout values.

gaps.title: Dependent-failure analysis
gaps.status: Drafted in this TSC (12 coupling factors); 3 open
gaps.next: Close shared limit values, environmental zone, and G1.

gaps.title: ASIL B/C alert and driver-monitoring requirements run on QM hardware and Linux
gaps.next: Choose per goal: develop the alert path to the required ASIL, decompose with the panda's independent siren (TSR-ALR-05) as the second channel, or revisit the ratings. Driver monitoring also needs ISO/PAS 8800 for the model.

gaps.title: panda platform firmware shares the MCU with the checker without memory protection
gaps.next: Develop SP05 to ASIL D or show freedom from interference: enable the Cortex-M7 MPU around safety state, and analyze it in the DFA.
